name: 黃如瑩
objective:
This course is designed to develop upper-intermediate to advanced lexical competence in EFL learners through sustained engagement with authentic and literary sources. Drawing on film, canonical literature, BBC news media, and celebrated dramatic soliloquies, students will encounter vocabulary in the full richness of its cultural and emotional context. Rather than treating words as isolated units of information, the course cultivates a deep awareness of connotation, register, collocation, and rhetorical effect. By the end of the semester, students will have acquired practical target vocabulary items and useful idiomatic expressions, and will demonstrate the ability to deploy this lexicon with accuracy and confidence in both written and spoken discourse.

此課程旨在協助學生建立相當於美國大學入學測驗的高階字彙，亦即相當於接受高等教育之英語系國家人士所具備的用字能力。此課程將通過故事方式介紹此類字彙，其中也包括字形學之解析。學生修習此課程後應能將高階字彙使用於正確的上下文中，因此可達成下列諸目的：
"	提昇高階字彙數量
"	加強英文閱讀能力
"	習得重要字源解析
"	避上下文中的用字錯誤
"	提高英語表達能力
"	加強英文寫作能力
"	精進英語文溝通技巧
This course aims to help students build a more powerful vocabulary on the SAT (the qualifying exam for US college admission) level, i.e. the level of proficiency of an educated native speaker's. Students will be introduced to the lexical use through story scenes. Morphological analysis of the words will be included in the course. At the exit of this course, students are expected to use them in their proper contexts and hence reach the following goals:
"	Develop a powerful vocabulary
"	Improve reading skills
"	Learn important word roots
"	Avoid word usage error in context
"	Become a better speaker
"	Strengthen his / her writing ability
"	Improve communication skills
schedule:
1.	Course: Advanced Vocabulary (for B1+ and B2+ EFL students) 
2.	Text sources: Film clips, literary passages, BBC News videos, soliloquies and great speeches
3.	Syllabus 
Week 1 — Introduction Week
Focus: Vocabulary learning strategies; self-assessment; establishing word banks
Activity: Vocabulary Levels Test; introduction to word maps, context-guessing, collocation notebooks, and vocabulary journals
No target list: diagnostic and methodological week

Unit 1: Identity and belonging (film clips)
Week 2 — Dead Poets Society (1989)
Clip: "Carpe Diem" opening classroom scene (~4 min) 
Week 3 — The Devil Wears Prada (2006)
Clip: Miranda's cerulean sweater monologue (~3 min) 
Week 4 — The Pursuit of Happiness (2006)
Clip: "Don't ever let somebody tell you you can't do something" (~2 min)

Unit 2: Human nature and society (literary passages) 
Week 5 — The Great Gatsby: Chapter 1 excerpt (Fitzgerald)
Focus: Descriptive/evaluative vocabulary; social class
Week 6 — Animal Farm: Chapter 1 (Orwell)
Focus: Political/rhetorical vocabulary
Week 7 — Never Let Me Go: Chapter 1 excerpt (Kazuo Ishiguro)
Focus: Memory, identity, and loss; culturally resonant for Asian students

Unit 3: The World Today (BBC News Videos) 
Week 8 — Topic: climate and environment
Source: BBC Learning English, "6 Minute English" environmental episodes 
Week 9 — Topic: technology and society
Source: BBC Learning English, "6 Minute English" AI/technology episodes 

Week 10 — Midterm Exam
Format: Vocabulary-in-context gap fill, idiom matching, collocation quiz, short paragraph using target words from previous units

Unit 4: Emotion and ethics (film clips) 
Week 11 — Schindler's List (1993)
Clip: "I could have got more…" breakdown scene (~4 min) 
Week 12 — Inside Out (2015)
Clip: Joy and Sadness discuss core memories (~5 min) 

Unit 5: The art of the spoken word (soliloquies and great speeches)  
Week 13 — Shakespeare: Hamlet – "To Be or Not to Be" (Act III, Scene 1)
Performance clips: Kenneth Branagh (1996), David Tennant (2009), Benedict Cumberbatch (2015) — all on YouTube
Week 14 — (1) Jane Austen: Pride and Prejudice – Mr. Darcy's First Proposal (Ch. 34) and (2) Jane Eyre's "I Am No Bird" Speech (Ch. 23, Brontë)
Film clips: (1) 2005 *Pride and Prejudice (Keira Knightley); (2) 2011 Jane Eyre (Mia Wasikowska) — both on YouTube
Focus: Romantic/social vocabulary; gender and power; contrast between entitled passion and fierce equality
Week 15 — (1) Charlie Chaplin: The Great Dictator – Final Speech (1940); (2) Atticus Finch: To Kill a Mockingbird – Closing Argument
Film clip: Chaplin's speech on YouTube (public domain)
Focus: justice, democracy, and humanity; formal rhetorical register

Unit 6: Identity, culture and change (BBC News Videos) 
Week 16 — Topic: language and identity; gender and social roles
Source: BBC Learning English – "6 Minute English" bilingual/identity; gender equality episodes
Week 17 — Vocabulary Portfolio Presentations
Students present a personal word bank of 50 words from the semester with:
- Original sentences demonstrating contextual use
- Collocations and word family variants
- A 2-minute spoken mini-speech using 5 chosen words (recorded or live)
- A short written reflection on where and how each word was encountered

Week 18 — Final Exam
Format: Authentic reading passage; vocabulary-in-use test; idiom interpretation section; short essay (200–250 words) incorporating vocabulary from all units
scorePolicy:
Grading: Percentile of final grades 
(1) Midterm Exam (Week 10):  25% 
(2) Final Exam (Week 18): 30% 
(3) Weekly vocabulary quizzes: 20% 
(4) Portfolio presentation (Week 17): 15% 
(5) Participation & in-class tasks: 10%
